options.a: Both firms would jointly be better off if they could each keep their prices high.
options.b: There is no dominant strategy in this game.
options.c: This game has a Nash equilibrium: Both firms don't lower their prices.
options.d: If firm 1 lowers its prices and firm 2 does not, firm 1 will earn a profit of €20000.

questions.text: In long-run equilibrium in a competitive market,

options.a: firms are operating at the minimum of their average total cost curves.
options.b: firms are operating at their efficient scale.
options.c: firms are operating at zero economic profit.
options.d: firms are operating at the intersection of their marginal cost and marginal revenue curve.
options.e: All of these answers are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about monopolistic competition is correct?

options.a: A monopolistically competitive firm has some power to set the price of its product because there are barriers to entry.
options.b: One difference between perfect competition and monopolistic competition is that firms in monopolistic competition face a downward-sloping demand curve.
options.c: In the short run, a monopolistically competitive firm chooses its quantity, but not its price.
options.d: Firms in monopolistic competition always will earn an economic profit.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is false?

options.a: If the rate at which goods can be substituted in production is constant, then the production possibility frontier exhibits constant opportunity costs.
options.b: The process observed when an economy's production possibility frontier shifts outward is comparative advantage.
options.c: If the amount of resources available to the local economy increases, or there are improvements in technology, then the production possibility frontier will shift outward.
options.d: Because of trade, a country may produce at a point outside its production possibility frontier.
options.e: A country is said to have a comparative advantage in the production of a good if it has the lowest opportunity cost of producing that good compared with other economies.

questions.text: Which of the following events will shift the demand curve for watches to the right?

options.a: A decrease in the price of batteries if batteries and watches are complements.
options.b: A decrease in consumer incomes if watches are a normal good.
options.c: A decrease in the wage of workers employed to manufacture watches.
options.d: A decrease in the price of watches.
options.e: An advance in the technology used to manufacture watches.

questions.text: Which of the following is a problem of adverse selection?

options.a: Sellers (who know more than buyers about the quality of their products) deliberately sell products of inferior quality.
options.b: Moral hazard in the market for lemons.
options.c: Only high-quality products are offered for sale.
options.d: The management of a company selects an employee who is not qualified for the position within the firm.
